author: Nguyen Dieu Tu Uyen, Nguyen Xuan Quynh
description: Vietnam’s Communist Party chief is set to take the stage Tuesday at the opening ceremony for the National Congress in Hanoi, a forum where the ruling party of the fast-growing Southeast Asian nation will sign off on a new five-year development plan.
title: Vietnam’s Lam Takes Spotlight as Party Selects New Leadership

author: Ellen Milligan
description: The UK appeared to lay the groundwork for approving China’s new embassy in London on the eve of a controversial decision that risks driving a deeper wedge both within the ruling Labour party and with the US administration.
title: UK Lays Groundwork for Approval of Controversial Chinese Embassy

author: Thomas Seal
description: China doesn’t hold the solution for Canada’s economic issues and isn’t a trustworthy partner, Taiwan’s top representative to Ottawa said following Prime Minister Mark Carney’s tariff deal with Xi Jinping.
title: China Isn’t the Answer for Canada’s Trade Troubles, Taiwan Envoy Says

author: Kirsi Heikel
description: Finland’s President Alexander Stubb said he is worried the crisis over Greenland will “suck out all the oxygen” at the World Economic Forum in Davos, sidelining Russia’s war in Ukraine.
title: Greenland Risks Sucking Out All the Oxygen at Davos, Stubb Says

author: Carla Canivete
description: US President Donald Trump invited a slew of world leaders to join his ‘Board of Peace for Gaza,’ as he hopes to advance his 20-point plan to ensure a lasting peace and reconstruction of the Palestinian enclave.
title: The List of People Invited to Trump’s Board of Peace for Gaza

author: Nduka Orjinmo
description: Armed bandits kidnapped more than 170 worshippers from two churches in Nigeria’s Kaduna state, the Daily Trust newspaper reported, citing witnesses.
title: More Than 170 Worshippers Abducted in Northern Nigeria, Daily Trust Says

author: Rachel Gamarski, Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazil Supreme Court Justice Dias Toffoli authorized the freezing of assets belonging to investor Nelson Tanure as part of an investigation into Banco Master SA, according to a Jan. 6 decision unsealed by the court on Friday.
title: Brazilian Judge Orders Tanure’s Assets Frozen in Banco Master Probe

author: Alex Wickham, Ellen Milligan, Joe Mayes
description: What was billed as an “emergency” Monday morning press conference offered Keir Starmer a now-or-never chance to hit back at Donald Trump over his latest assault on the transatlantic alliance.
title: Starmer’s ‘Love Actually’ Moment With Trump May Never Come

author: Alexander Weber, Mark Schroers
description: Croatia’s central-bank chief, Boris Vujcic, is set to become the next European Central Bank vice president — and the first person from eastern Europe to join the institution’s Executive Board.
title: ECB No. 2 Job Race Won by Vujcic in Victory for Eastern Europe

author: Ania Nussbaum
description: President Emmanuel Macron does not plan to accept US President Donald Trump’s invitation to join a proposed Board of Peace, according to a person close to the French leader.
title: Macron to Decline Trump’s Invitation to Join His ‘Peace Board’

author: Slav Okov
description: Bulgarian President Rumen Radev announced his resignation as the country prepares for its eighth national election in five years, fueling speculation that he may enter the fray to end the entrenched political deadlock.
title: Bulgarian President to Resign, Hints He May Run in Snap Vote

author: Mark Schroers, Jana Randow, Jorge Valero
description: Croatia’s Boris Vujcic is heading for victory in the race for the European Central Bank vice presidency with only Finland’s Olli Rehn left to beat after two rounds of voting by finance ministers, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
title: Croatia’s Vujcic Closes in on ECB No. 2 Job in Tussle With Rehn

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi
description: Ukrainian authorities are pressing ahead with a tax on self-employed entrepreneurs, one of the most contentious policies demanded by the International Monetary Fund to unlock more than $8 billion in wartime financing.
title: Ukraine to Move Forward With Contentious Tax Bill Sought by IMF

author: Matthew Malinowski
description: Chilean President-elect José Antonio Kast will inherit a crisis as raging wildfires killed at least 19 people over the weekend and left hundreds homeless, setting up a lengthy reconstruction process on his administration’s watch.
title: Chile’s Incoming President Inherits Crisis as Raging Wildfires Kill 19

author: Jana Randow
description: Europe must urgently complete long-delayed infrastructure projects that are critical to economic competitiveness and resilience as geopolitical tensions linger, according to the European Court of Auditors.
title: EU Is Decades Behind, Billions Above Plan on Key Transport Links

author: Matthew Boesler
description: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said it’s too early to gauge the economic impact of tensions over Greenland, though it could be a headwind for growth.
title: IMF’s Georgieva Says Tensions Over Greenland Could Curb Growth

author: Alex Wickham, Alberto Nardelli
description: US President Donald Trump’s proposed Board of Peace has got off to a rough start: questioned by Europe, criticized by Israel and celebrated by friends of the Kremlin.
title: Trump’s Peace Board Faces Rewrite Calls After Messy Start

author: Lucille Liu, Daniel Flatley
description: Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, the nation’s economic czar and top trade negotiator, is scheduled to meet with a group of global CEOs while attending the World Economic Forum, according to a person familiar with the matter.
title: China’s Top Trade Negotiator Slated to Meet Global CEOs in Davos

author: William Horobin
description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will use Article 49.3 of the constitution to pass the delayed 2026 budget without a parliamentary vote, according to news channel BFM TV.
title: French Premier to End Budget Drama and Bypass Parliament Vote

author: Gresa Kraja
description: Kosovo’s election commission on Monday ordered a full recount of votes from last month’s snap elections after discrepancies were found in results for individual candidates in some municipalities.
title: Kosovo Commission Orders Full Recount of December Elections

author: Arsalan Shahla
description: Top Iranian officials called for “leniency and compassion” for some of the protesters arrested during the latest wave of unrest, despite a pledge from the police to continue cracking down on dissenters.
title: Iran Softens Rhetoric on Protesters as Police Continue Crackdown

author: Michael Nienaber
description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he’s trying to persuade French President Emmanuel Macron to tone down his response to US President Donald Trump’s latest threat to slap new trade tariffs on European allies.
title: Merz Seeks to Rein In Macron in Response to Trump Tariff Threat

author: William Horobin
description: France is seeking to convene a meeting of Group of Seven finance chiefs as soon Wednesday to discuss US President Donald Trump’s threat to hit allies with additional tariffs for opposing his bid to annex Greenland.
title: France Plans G-7 Meeting to Talk US Tariff Threats on Wednesday

author: Layan Odeh
description: The head of Picton Investments said bond markets will swiftly discipline the US if President Donald Trump appoints a Federal Reserve chair who’s seen as too malleable — and precious metals remain a good hedge against political volatility.
title: Hedge Fund Picton Says Markets Will Punish a Fed That Bows to Trump

author: Katarina Hoije, Souhail Karam
description: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye declared a public holiday following the national football team’s victory at the Africa Cup of Nations championship Sunday, providing a morale boost to a country grappling with a debt crisis.
title: Senegal Celebrates Football Victory While Navigating Debt Talks

author: Laura Alviz
description: TKMS AG& Co KGaA Chief Financial Officer Paul Glaser said the crisis unfolding over Greenland might help the company’s chances of winning a multi-billion euro submarine contract with Canada, as Ottawa considers a stronger relationship with Europe amid US tensions.
title: TKMS CFO Says Greenland Crisis Could Help Deal For Canada Subs

author: Christian Wienberg, Sanne Wass
description: Danish officials have decided not to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos this week amid an intensifying dispute over Greenland that’s shaking transatlantic relations.
title: Danish Officials Set to Skip Davos as Greenland Spat Escalates

author: Brendan Murray
description: President Donald Trump’s duties on imported goods are paid almost entirely by American importers, their domestic customers and ultimately US consumers, a study from a German think tank concluded.
title: Americans Bear Almost All the Cost of Trump Tariffs, Study Shows

author: Paul Vecchiatto, Michael Cohen
description: South Africa’s government is facing mounting pressure to explain Iran’s participation in naval drills off the coast of Cape Town, a move that has further soured Pretoria’s already fractious ties with the US.
title: South Africa Faces Mounting Furor Over Iran Role in Naval Drills

author: Marilen Martin
description: Germany’s €3 billion ($3.5 billion) subsidy program for electric vehicles will be open to all manufacturers, including Chinese brands, as the government seeks to revive sales in Europe’s largest car market.
title: Germany’s €3 Billion EV Subsidy Will Be Open to Chinese Brands

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Giorgia Meloni is positioning herself as mediator between Europe and President Donald Trump over Greenland, suggesting the US may have misinterpreted European moves to send troops to the Arctic island.
title: Meloni Offers to Be Europe’s Mediator With Trump on Greenland

author: Flavia Krause-Jackson
description: After months of trying and failing to satisfy the US leader, European officials need to decide how robustly to respond to his latest threats over Greenland.
title: Europe’s Appeasement of Donald Trump Runs Out of Road

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has received an invitation to join Donald Trump’s proposed Board of Peace for Gaza, the Kremlin said.
title: Trump Invited Putin to Join Gaza ‘Board of Peace,’ Kremlin Says

author: John Liu, Yujing Liu, Fran Wang, Nectar Gan
description: As Xi Jinping battles unprecedented deflation and shrinking investment, he’s betting that China can sell more and more goods to the world to drive growth. To that end, Donald Trump’s threats against key US allies are coming at a good time.
title: Xi’s Export Machine Gets Lift From US Move to Strongarm Allies

description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer says US President Donald Trump’s threat to impose tariffs on the UK and other European nations over the Greenland issue is “completely wrong” and that “a trade war is in no one’s interests.” He made the comments at a news conference at 10 Downing Street.
title: Starmer Says Trump’s Tariffs Threat ‘Completely Wrong’

author: Alex Wickham, Joe Mayes
description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer took a stand against President Donald Trump’s threats of new tariffs on European nations and said they would damage the British economy.
title: Starmer Rebukes Trump Threats as ‘Completely Wrong’ From an Ally

author: Michael Nienaber, Kamil Kowalcze
description: US President Donald Trump’s threat to annex Greenland is a red line for the European Union and the 27-nation bloc should consider using a legal mechanism designed to repel economic coercion, according to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil.
title: Germany Says Trump Has Reached Red Line With Greenland Threat

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, equity futures fell, while gold and silver surged to records after Donald Trump proposed new tariffs on eight European countries over Greenland.

EU leaders will hold an emergency meeting on Trump’s tariff threat in the coming days as member states weigh retaliatory measures including levies on €93 billion of US goods and use of the anti-coercion instrument.

China’s economy grew 5% in 2025, meeting the government target. Industrial production climbed in December while retail sales grew at the slowest pace since the Covid reopening.

Today's guests: Valérie Noël, Head of Trading at Syz Group. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Rocks Europe, EU Weighs Greenland Tariff Retaliation | Daybreak Europe 01/19/2026

author: Yian Lee
description: China sent a military drone into Taiwanese airspace for the first time, underscoring Beijing’s efforts to test the self-run democracy’s defenses.
title: China Sends Military Drone Into Taiwan Airspace for First Time

author: Randy Thanthong-Knight
description: With the birth rate in Thailand falling fast, one political party jockeying for position ahead of the country’s snap election next month reckons it has the answer: step in to help citizens find love.
title: Thai Political Party Floats State Matchmaking to Fix Birth Rates

author: Alberto Nardelli, Heidi Taksdal Skjeseth
description: Donald Trump linked his claims on Greenland to not being awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in a letter the US president sent to Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store.
title: Trump Links Greenland Threats to Nobel Peace Prize Snub

description: Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair distanced himself from US President Donald Trump’s demand that countries pay $1 billion for permanent membership to the Board of Peace. Blair, who’s been appointed to the executive panel of the Board of Peace, declined to endorse the request for the funds. Some countries would likely refuse to join the Board as a result of Trump’s terms, people familiar with the matter said. Bloomberg’s Dan Williams reports.
title: Blair Distances Himself From $1 Bln Board of Peace Fee

author: Matthew Hill
description: Mozambican President Daniel Chapo canceled a trip to the World Economic Forum in Davos after floods in the southern African nation killed dozens of people and left tens of thousands of houses damaged or destroyed.
title: Mozambique Leader Chapo Cancels Davos Trip as Dozens Killed in Floods

description: The European Union is in talks to potentially impose tariffs on €93 billion ($108 billion) of US goods if President Donald Trump follows through on his threat to hit European countries with a 10% levy. Trump announced a 10% tariff on goods from eight European countries starting in February, rising to 25% in June, unless there’s a deal for the “purchase of Greenland.” Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports.
title: European Leaders React to Trump’s 10% Tariff Threat

author: Jon Herskovitz
description: President Donald Trump called a New York Stock Exchange equities trading outpost in Texas “an UNBELIEVABLY BAD THING” for New York and a “big test” for Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who took office earlier this month.
title: Trump Says Mamdani Facing ‘Big Test’ From NYSE’s Texas Trading Outpost

author: Zoe Schneeweiss, Mark Schroers
description: Euro-area finance ministers are set to select the European Central Bank’s next vice president on Monday in a decision that will set the stage for the succession to Christine Lagarde in the top job.
title: Euro Area to Pick ECB’s No. 2 in Prelude to Bigger Board Revamp

description: For more than four decades, Jeremy Grantham has been one of the most contrarian voices in global investing. The co-founder of Boston-based asset manager GMO, he built his reputation warning about bubbles before they burst, from Japanese equities in the late 1980s to US tech stocks in 2000 and housing in the run-up to the global financial crisis. He joins this week’s Merryn Talks Money podcast with host Merryn Somerset Webb to discuss why he believes there's an artificial intelligence bubble and what happens if it bursts, his approach as a value investor and the lessons in his new book, "The Making of a Permabear: The Perils of Long-Term Investing in a Short-Term World." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: GMO's Jeremy Grantham Sees an AI Bubble — and a Familiar Ending

author: Jorge Valero, Alberto Nardelli
description: The European Union is in talks to potentially impose tariffs on €93 billion ($108 billion) of US goods if President Donald Trump follows through on his threat to hit European countries with a 10% levy on Feb. 1.
title: EU Eyes Tariffs on €93 Billion of US Goods Over New Trump Threat

author: Jing Li
description: China’s birth rate fell last year to its lowest level since 1949, highlighting a deepening demographic struggle for Beijing even as officials roll out new subsidies to encourage couples to have more children.
title: China Birth Rate Hits Lowest Since 1949 in Blow to Baby Drive

author: Andreo Calonzo
description: An impeachment complaint was filed against Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the House of Representatives, which is dominated by his allies.
title: Philippines’ Marcos Faces Impeachment Attempt at Ally-Led House

author: Irina Anghel
description: Home-sellers in the UK have ramped up their asking prices at the sharpest pace in more than a decade, according to new data, as confidence returns to the property market following the Labour government’s autumn budget.
title: Prices of UK Homes Listed for Sale Soar After Reeves Budget

author: Isabella Ward
description: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves is set to say critics of the UK’s capital markets “were wrong” and herald “a new golden age for the City” at the London Stock Exchange on Monday, as new rules to make it easier to raise public capital in Britain kick in.
title: Reeves Says London IPO Critics Were ‘Wrong’ as New Rules Kick In

author: Tom Rees
description: Britain is seeing early signs of a long-awaited turnaround of its productivity woes, according to an alternative measure that suggests output per hour worked has risen at a pace not seen since before the financial crisis.
title: UK Productivity Surge Signals Economic Turnaround, Study Finds
